signature.instructions:
Identify the political committee that sponsored a fundraising email.

The committee's name is present in the email text itself. Return the exact legal name of the sponsoring committee as it appears in the 'Paid for by' disclaimer, with no trailing address, disclaimer, or unsubscribe text.

module_src:
class IdentifyCommitteeModule(dspy.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fallback = dspy.Predict(dspy.Signature('email_body: str -> committee: str', "Identify the political committee that sponsored a fundraising email.\n\nThe committee's name is present in the email text itself. Return the exact legal name of the sponsoring committee as it appears in the 'Paid for by' disclaimer, with no trailing address, disclaimer, or unsubscribe text."))

    def forward(self, **inputs):
        import re

        email_body = inputs.get("email_body", "") or ""

        def clean(name):
            name = name.strip()
            name = name.strip(" .,;:")
            name = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", name)
            return name.strip()

        def dedupe(candidate):
            # Handle cases where the name is repeated, e.g.
            # "Shontel Brown for Congress Shontel Brown for Congress" or
            # duplication where the second copy is followed by trailing junk.
            words = candidate.split(" ")
            n = len(words)
            # exact doubling
            if n >= 2 and n % 2 == 0:
                half = n // 2
                if words[:half] == words[half:]:
                    return " ".join(words[:half])
            # A copy that repeats: find first occurrence of a repeat of the start.
            # Look for the earliest index i>=1 where words[i:] starts with words[:i]
            # AND words[:i] looks like a complete committee name.
            return candidate

        def looks_like_name_end(word):
            # Words that typically end a committee name.
            enders = {
                "congress", "senate", "president", "committee",
                "victory", "fund", "pac", "inc", "llc", "revolution",
                "america", "americans", "party", "campaign", "council",
            }
            return word.lower().strip(".,") in enders

        def extract_paid_for_by(text):
            # Find "Paid for by" (case-insensitive) and capture until a terminator.
            m = re.search(r"[Pp]aid [Ff]or [Bb]y\s+(.*)", text, re.DOTALL)
            if not m:
                return None
            tail = m.group(1)

            # Cut at strong terminating markers.
            cut_patterns = [
                r"\bNot authorized\b",
                r"\bP\.?\s?O\.?\s*(?:Box|BOX)\b",
                r"\bPO Box\b",
                r"https?://",
                r"\bwww\.",
                r"\bclick here\b",
                r"\bThis email\b",
                r"\bEmails like\b",
                r"\bMilitary images\b",
                r"\bunsubscribe\b",
                r"\bwhy did I get this\b",
                r"\bIf you\b",
                r"\bDonations\b",
                r"\bmailto:",
                r"[\[\]|]",
                r"\n",
                r"\d{2,}",  # any 2+ digit number (address/zip)
                r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@",  # email address
            ]
            end = len(tail)
            for pat in cut_patterns:
                mm = re.search(pat, tail, re.IGNORECASE)
                if mm and mm.start() < end:
                    end = mm.start()
            candidate = tail[:end]

            candidate = clean(candidate)
            if not candidate:
                return None

            # Sometimes text like "Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe" gets
            # partially through; if there's a duplicated all-caps repeat of the
            # name, keep the shortest valid prefix. Try to trim at a natural end word.
            words = candidate.split(" ")
            # Find the last "ender" word within a reasonable prefix and cut there
            # only if trailing words don't look like part of a name.
            # First, try exact dedup.
            candidate = dedupe(candidate)
            words = candidate.split(" ")

            # If the candidate is long (> 6 words), try to trim to the first
            # natural committee-name ending.
            if len(words) > 6:
                for i, w in enumerate(words):
                    if looks_like_name_end(w):
                        candidate = " ".join(words[:i + 1])
                        break

            candidate = clean(candidate)
            return candidate if candidate else None

        def is_confident(name):
            # A confident committee name: reasonable length, no junk tokens.
            if not name:
                return False
            words = name.split(" ")
            if len(words) < 2 or len(words) > 8:
                return False
            low = name.lower()
            bad_markers = [
                "http", "www.", "click here", "unsubscribe", "@", "email",
                "images", "why did", "donations", "not authorized", "[", "]",
                "|", "po box", "p.o.",
            ]
            if any(b in low for b in bad_markers):
                return False
            if re.search(r"\d", name):
                return False
            # Ends in a recognizable committee-name word.
            if looks_like_name_end(words[-1]):
                return True
            # Otherwise not confident enough.
            return False

        result = extract_paid_for_by(email_body)

        if is_confident(result):
            return dspy.Prediction(committee=result)

        # Fallback to LM when deterministic extraction is not confident.
        pred = self.fallback(email_body=email_body)
        return dspy.Prediction(committee=str(pred.committee).strip())
